paper_metadata.title: Effect of Temperature on the Structure and Mechanical Properties of Zr–2.5% Nb Alloy Processed by Rotary Forging
paper_metadata.journal: Transactions of the Indian Institute of Metals

evidence.quote: The influence of the temperature of the rotary forging process as well as the temperature of the post-deformation annealing on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the Zr–2.5% Nb zirconium alloy was studied.

The formation of the ultrafine-grained structure in the Zr–2.5% Nb alloy led to a significant increase in its tensile strength characteristics at ambient temperature compared to the recrystallized alloy

Rotary forging of the Zr–2.5%Nb alloy at a temperature of both 200 and 300 °C provides a comparable increase in strength (about 2 times), while the alloy after rotary forging at a temperature of 300 °C has a higher ductility.
One of the most common commercial high-strength zirconium alloys is Zr–2.5% Nb (E125) [5 ].
the microstructure and mechanical properties of the Zr–2.5% Nb zirconium alloy was studied.

Rotary forging of the as recrystallized Zr–2.5% Nb alloy workpiece from an initial diameter of 12 mm to a final diameter of 6.5 mm was carried out using a modernized two-die rotary forging machine V2129.01.
The ultimate tensile strength of the alloy after RF at both temperatures is comparable (810–815 MPa) which is 1.6 times higher than the ultimate tensile strength of the recrystallized alloy.
The 0.2%-yield strength of the alloy after RF at a temperature of 300 °C is slightly lower than its 0.2%-yield strength after RF at a temperature of 200 °C: 600–615 MPa and 630–660 MPa, respectively

Rotary forging of the as recrystallized Zr–2.5% Nb alloy workpiece from an initial diameter of 12 mm to a final diameter of 6.5 mm was carried out using a modernized two-die rotary forging machine V2129.01.
As a result of RF of the original workpieces with a true strain e = 1.22, their length increased to 2000 mm.
The workpieces before forging and between passes were heated to two temperatures, namely (1) 200ºC and (2) 300ºC.
